stories.title: Passkey Sign-In Gate, Step-Up Re-Verification & Owner Guard
stories.description: Re-groomed 2026-09-25 (split from the original 8-point hardening story; session management, alerts and browser hardening moved to STORY-118). Passkeys are optional, but once a user has one it is required at every sign-in, so a stolen Discord account alone cannot reach the dashboard. Removing a passkey needs a fresh passkey check. Sensitive writes (owner console, integrations, moderation escalation policy, reaction-role publishing) always need a passkey check newer than 5 minutes, so users without a passkey cannot perform them. Bot owners (BOT_OWNER_ID) must have a passkey. Recovery is an operator CLI reset, not recovery codes. Sessions stay opaque and server-side: JWE was re-evaluated and rejected again because a stolen token is replayed, not decrypted (ADR-013).

stories.title: Session Management, Sign-In & Change Alerts, Browser Hardening & Authorization Coverage
stories.description: Split from STORY-117 on 2026-09-25. Makes a stolen session visible and killable (active sessions page, new-device and passkey-removal DMs, dashboard change notices in the guild log channel) and hardens the browser side (nonce CSP, security headers, React taint, rate limits) with a test that fails if any Server Action or route handler skips its guard. Risk-based re-checks on IP or user-agent changes were considered and dropped: an infostealer copies the device cookie together with the session cookie, and IP binding misfires for mobile and VPN users.

stories.title: Chrome Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) for Dashboard Sessions
stories.description: Optional enhancement from ADR-013 decision 4, parked 2026-09-25. Where the browser supports DBSC, bind the dashboard session to a TPM-held key and issue short-lived cookies that must be refreshed with a signature, so a cookie copied by malware stops working within minutes. Groomed 2026-10-04: DBSC is generally available in Chrome 146 on Windows (April 2026) and the spec is a W3C Working Draft; macOS support is coming. Re-estimated from 3 to 8 points and split into TASK-1191 (protocol core) and TASK-1192 (routes, wiring, UI, docs). Browsers without DBSC keep the current behavior; a bound session cannot be downgraded.

stories.title: Unified Configurable Reset Boundary & Consecutive-Miss Streak Forgiveness
stories.description: Replace the five independent UTC calendar-day resets with one shared configurable reset boundary (default 00:00 GMT+8), exposed through a core ResetSchedule helper returning an integer day index. Covers energy replenishment, the energy potion daily ceiling, TCG shop daily rotation, the economy shop daily purchase limit and /daily. Converts /daily from a rolling 24h cooldown with 12h grace into a calendar-day claim with consecutive-miss streak forgiveness: fewer consecutive missed days than the configured threshold preserve the streak (missed days are skipped, never counted), reaching the threshold wipes the streak and the triggering claim counts as day 1. Missed count is derived from lastDailyAt rather than persisted. One global timezone offset with per-feature clock-time overrides.

tasks.title: DBSC Protocol Core: web_sessions Binding Columns, Proof Verification, Sealed Challenges & Bound Cookie

codegraph_queries: SessionService resolve completePasskeyCheck listForUser SessionSummary isLive toActiveSession

acceptance: web_sessions has nullable dbsc_session_id (unique) and dbsc_public_key columns in both the SQLite and PostgreSQL schemas, and the generated DDL is regenerated with db:generate-ddl.
WebSessionRepository can find a session by dbsc_session_id; repository tests cover it on SQLite.

apps/web/src/lib/server/auth/dbsc.ts verifies a dbsc+jwt proof with node:crypto only (ES256 with ieee-p1363 signatures, RS256): it rejects alg none, other algs, a wrong typ, a missing or invalid jwk on registration, a bad signature, and a jti that is not a valid, fresh sealed challenge for the expected session.

Challenges and the bound cookie are vault-sealed {sid, exp} values under distinct vault contexts (challenge TTL 2 minutes, bound cookie 10 minutes); helpers build the Secure-Session-Registration and Secure-Session-Challenge header values and the session instructions JSON (session_identifier, refresh_url, scope with include_site false, credentials for __Host-ririko_bound with Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax).

SessionService.bindDevice verifies the registration proof, refuses an already bound session, stores a random dbsc_session_id and the JWK, and rotates the session ID through a private helper shared with completePasskeyCheck (Discord tokens re-encrypted).
SessionService.refreshBinding returns a challenge when no proof is given, a new bound cookie for a valid proof signed by the stored key, and a not-found result for an unknown or expired session.

SessionService.resolve(token, boundCookie) returns null for a bound session without a valid, unexpired bound cookie for its dbsc_session_id; an unbound session resolves as before. listForUser reports deviceBound.
Unit tests use EC P-256 and RSA keys generated in the test and cover every rejection above plus the full register, challenge, refresh, resolve flow.

bugs.title: Passkey Sign-In Check Rejected Authenticators Without the User-Verification Flag; Failures Were Unlogged and Escaped as Unhandled Errors
bugs.description: Reported 2026-09-25: the passkey check failed with 'The passkey could not be verified' in Edge while registration worked. Root cause: the authenticator Edge used signed assertions without the user-verification (UV) flag, and verification required it. The reason was invisible because verification failures were not logged. Two more defects hid it: getWebServices() cached services on globalThis, so after a hot reload the server kept running old code, and its PasskeyVerificationError class no longer matched the action's instanceof check, so failures escaped as unhandled rejections. Fix: request UV but only require user presence (the passkey is a second factor after Discord sign-in), return passkey outcomes instead of throwing, log every rejection reason, and cache only the database connection process-wide.

bugs.title: Auto Voice Deleted Every Empty Voice Channel in a Join-to-Create Hub's Category, Including Permanent Server Channels
bugs.description: Reported 2026-09-26: AutoVoiceService deleted any empty voice channel in the category of a join-to-create hub, not only the temporary channels it created. Both the member-leave handler and cleanupOrphans (run on READY) matched channels by category, and the set of created channels lived only in memory, so after a restart the bot could not tell its channels from the server's own. A guild with permanent voice channels next to a hub lost them whenever they were empty. Fix: persist the IDs of created channels in a new dual-dialect auto_voice_channels table (AutoVoiceChannelRepository), delete only recorded channels, forget records when the channel is deleted or no longer exists (including the channelDelete gateway event), and make cleanupOrphans iterate the records instead of scanning the category. Existing databases need pnpm db:push.

bugs.title: Shared Row Types Say number but Postgres Returns bigint for Balances and XP
bugs.description: Found in TASK-1241 when the repository suites first ran on Postgres. The shared row types in packages/database/src/schema/types/index.ts (EconomyBalance, EconomyTransaction, XpAccount and others) are inferred from the SQLite schema, so they declare number. The Postgres schema uses bigint({ mode: "bigint" }) for wallet/bank balances, net worth, transaction amounts and XP, so the same repository methods return bigint on Postgres. Callers wrap the values in Number() or BigInt() today, but plain arithmetic or JSON serialisation of a raw value throws on Postgres only. Fix by normalising in the repositories (or typing the values as bigint everywhere) and drop the Number() wrappers added to repositories.test.ts.

codegraph_queries: EconomyBalance EconomyTransaction XpAccount schema types index.ts pg bigint mode walletBalance netWorth
modifyBalance transferBalance addXp BigInt adventure-payout reward-rank

acceptance: Every Postgres bigint column uses { mode: 'number' }, so the rows match the shared types. The columns stay BIGINT and PG_SCHEMA_DDL is unchanged.
Repository and service code no longer converts to or from bigint for these columns; raw-SQL paths that read them (adventure payouts, reward ranks) return numbers on both dialects.
A describeDialects test reads a balance, a transaction, an XP account and a market listing on Postgres and asserts typeof number; plain arithmetic on them works.
pnpm test:postgres passes locally against postgres:16.
